constraints.statement: Keep the canvas focused on decisions.
constraints.reason: Supporting detail should be available without competing with the current question.

constraints.statement: Allow decisions to be revised as evidence changes.
constraints.reason: Early assumptions may change as the design develops.

nodes.title: Details on demand
nodes.question: Should supporting evidence open only when the reader asks for it?
nodes.agentRecommendation: Show the current response first and reveal supporting context when needed.

assumptions.statement: Most questions can be understood without opening every supporting example.

alternatives.title: Show everything inline
alternatives.description: Keep the answer, assumptions, and examples visible together. Less clicking, but a much longer panel.

alternatives.title: A separate reference document
alternatives.description: Keep detailed evidence in a document beside the tree. A quieter panel, but readers must connect the document to each question.

precedents.title: Brooks on using exemplars
precedents.insight: Prior designs can provide alternatives worth examining. Applying that idea here suggests keeping examples available beside the decision. This is a design principle, not evidence that this particular disclosure layout works.

precedents.title: Decision and recommendation boundaries (CONTEXT.md)
precedents.insight: The project glossary separates the user's submitted answer from the agent's proposal. This supports making the response primary. This is a product convention, not evidence from a usability study.

nodes.title: Find the right evidence
nodes.question: Should each consequential decision link to relevant examples?
nodes.agentRecommendation: Keep the comparison short and explain where the example differs.
nodes.notes: To investigate: Which existing project decisions offer a useful comparison?
